q: I take away her toys, I leave her in her room, I repeat “I won’t let you hit me” , I get down to her level, I speak in a quiet voice, I’ve spoken in a loud voice, she gets privileges taken away, etc. NOTHING works or gets through to her.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of an almost-3-year-old who screams, hits and kicks when refused; lists everything tried.

q: I have been crying every single day because I am just at my wits end. I feel like a complete failure.
cx: Same mother, months of hitting and screaming; says she cries daily.

q: The only thing that calms her down is me bringing her dad in. Then he talks to her and after awhile she will come out and apologize to me. I hate this so much.
cx: Only the father can calm the child; the mother hates needing him.

q: In the last two hours, the kids took apart the entire couch in the time it took me to wash and refill their water bottles.
cx: Mother 35 weeks pregnant with third child; 4.5- and 2.5-year-old suddenly ignore her.

q: They just stand there laughing and saying “you pick them up mama.” They took their clothes off and started sprinting around the house, knowing full well that I can’t catch them very easily right now.
cx: Pregnant mother describes the children dumping toys and running while she cannot chase them.

q: They ignore the sound of my voice altogether, and now it’s becoming the same with Dad… and both grandmas (who come to play regularly).
cx: The ignoring has spread from mother to father and to both grandmothers.

q: We’ve tried so many techniques, basically everything short of screaming and spanking. I’m starting to panic that this behavior is going to continue escalating and will only be worse after baby is born.
cx: Pregnant mother fears it gets worse once the third baby arrives.

q: having a stranger confirm that, yes, these are normal characteristics of kids this age is so grounding.
cx: Her reply to a commenter: what she wanted from strangers was confirmation it is normal.

q: We have taken quite a few things away over the last few weeks, various forms of “timeout”, quiet times, etc. […] They just find new things to dump out 😂
cx: Taking toys away and time-outs have not stopped the dumping.

q: Why the perfection outside of the home and near 100% accidents at home?
cx: Father of a 38-month-old, 4–6 months into potty training; dry outside, accidents at home.

q: Naked is not possible. We live in a pre-war in NYC with old hardwood floors that have gaps and such. No way to clean pee once it gets under there.
cx: Rejects the naked-at-home advice because of his apartment floors.

q: I can keep putting her on every hour but it also feels like because we're doing that she is relying on us to tell her when to go otherwise she just goes. […] I'm dying here.
cx: Hourly potty reminders made the child depend on being told.

q: Originally it was cashews after maybe two months. Then she locked down peeing. Turned to chocolate to try to close the book.
cx: Food rewards escalated as training stalled; chocolate stopped working too.

q: My wife is so busy with her work that she has dismissed my concerns especially because our daughter is starting daycare in August and I am more terrified after seeing her behaving like this.
cx: Work-from-home father; 19-month-old suddenly clings to him a month before daycare.

q: I got her her own today. She was super excited when I gave it to her after we got home.
cx: After a tantrum leaving a daycare toy behind, the parent bought the same toy (VTech Pull and Sing Puppy).

q: I told her it had to stay at school and she could play with it tomorrow. Cue the worst tantrum of her life-screaming at the top of her lungs, crying, red face, tears, the whole nine yards.
cx: Pickup from daycare; the child would not leave the daycare's toy.

q: We’ve tried zero pressure. We’ve tried lots of pressure. We’ve tried massive rewards, sticker charts, chocolates, even sleepover offers and general bribery.
cx: Father of a 3-year-old withholding for over a year, new baby sister at home; lists the tactics tried.

q: Even just the reassurance that we're not alone is probably all I came to this subreddit to ask for.
cx: Father thanks a commenter; says reassurance was what he came for.

q: It's almost just like where to start.
cx: After hundreds of replies, the father says the problem is not access to help but knowing where to start.

q: But, for my son to calm down, I have to reenact everything my husband did to the T.
cx: 3-year-old melts down when dad does any care; mother of him and a 10-month-old must redo it.

q: 6 months ago, be would have a tantrum but we would push through it in a few minutes (“I know you want Mama and that’s hard, but Dada is here to help you” Type of thing) and that would be it.
cx: The acknowledging script used to work; now the rage is stronger and they give in.

q: I love Unruffled and Janet Lansbury and RIE! I want to be this parent, I just have a hard time actually being this parent
cx: Mother knows the respectful-parenting material but cannot carry it out in the moment.

q: This response is really extreme and not helpful. While I understand we need to change what we’re doing, he doesn’t own us and he’s not the parent.
cx: Pushes back on a commenter who said the child runs the household.

q: “You are catering at a level that is unusual and I would stop.” - you could have just said that, thank you
cx: Wanted the blunt one-line verdict rather than a lecture.

q: Its great but she doesn't even call me mama anymore.
cx: Primary-caregiver mother of an 18-month-old who now wants only her father.

q: If she sits down and nothing comes out within a few seconds, she’s up. If I try to encourage her to stay another minute or read a book, she just says no. I don’t want to turn the potty into a battle.
cx: Day 5 of Oh Crap with a 23-month-old; good progress but won't sit.

q: Or is this all too much too early for her and we should pause and revisit again down the road?
cx: Same parent asks whether to stop and wait.

q: I noticed a few other kids (who might be a few months older btw) would kind of just stand 1-2 feet in front of their parents and watch the teacher and they were pretty chill. how do i get him to do that? lol
cx: First-time mother of a 14.5-month-old who runs off at a library programme.

q: I think i'm maybe feeling a little defeated too because I thought at this age I would start enjoying things with him but I feel like he's just too all over the place for us to really go anywhere and hang out..
cx: Same mother; outings are not what she imagined.
